name: Flare gas recovery and zero routine flaring
aliases: Zero routine flaring (flare gas recovery and small-scale GTL)
applications: capturing associated gas that would be flared
principle: Gas that would be burned in a flare is instead collected, compressed and treated so that it can be sold, used for power or reinjected. Vapour recovery units capture low-pressure methane streams from tanks and compressor seals. Where no pipeline exists, small-scale GTL or power generation can use the gas on site. Routine, non-emergency flaring can then be ended.

performance.metric: natural gas flared globally each year
performance.basis: majority is routine, non-emergency flaring; IEA 2025 tracker

performance.metric: hydrocarbon vapour capture by vapour recovery units
performance.basis: EPA Lessons Learned case study: vapor recovery can capture up to 95% of hydrocarbon vapors from tanks; recovered vapours usable as fuel or sale gas. Specific flare-gas-recovery-unit turndown figures were not found in open supplier datasheets

source.note: US EPA, Installing Vapor Recovery Units to Reduce Methane Losses (Lessons Learned), 2006 (read 2026-10-28)
IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, 2025 assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'Flare gas recovery' 9

advantages: Turns a waste stream into saleable gas
limitations: Needs a gas outlet or power use nearby
Small, remote flares may not justify compressors

gaps.item: capex per unit and payback with dollar year
